The def field of a row is read only to understand a route, never classified: 63,227 rows have a route equal to it, 23,743 a route that is its opening, 28,948 a route that stands inside it elsewhere, 221 carry the cut flag (axis: rows). The source's own key to its signs: none on file. The lane's copy of the source (the Sefaria dump of the Jastrow lexicon, 32,512 entries with 38,954 senses whose definitions are HTML, in <home>/Documents/999 footsteps/ledgers/work/ldmprs/source-cache/sefaria-dump-2026-07-14/jastrow-dictionary-entries.jsonl) carries no front matter and no list of abbreviations; the works-own-stamp strand holds nothing of this source; so every shape whose meaning rests on a sign convention begins "unverified:". What the copy shows is the source's structure: each sense's English wordings stand in italics, and a route is such an italic stretch: of the 27,076 distinct texts 22,573 equal one italic stretch of the source exactly, 28 equal one once their final mark is removed, 258 are the opening of a longer italic stretch, and 4,217 are not found as an italic stretch (axis: texts; the audit script is builder/source-audit.mjs, evidence about the source and no part of any test). In the source 12,896 of its 39,759 italic stretches hold a comma and 2,314 a semicolon (axis: stretches): the commas and semicolons of a route stand inside one sense's own wording, which is the ask's second-sentence case.

definitions.terms: In every test: a letter is any character of Unicode category L (JavaScript \p{L}); an uppercase letter is \p{Lu} and a lowercase letter \p{Ll}; a digit is \p{N}; whitespace is what JavaScript's \s matches; to trim is what JavaScript's String.trim does; a word is a maximal run of characters that are not whitespace, unless a test says a run of letters; the run of letters before a mark is the maximal run of letters, apostrophes (U+0027) and right single quotation marks (U+2019) that ends directly before it. 'Directly before' and 'directly after' name the adjacent character, whitespace counted as a character; 'the end of the text' means that only whitespace, or nothing, follows. Every match against a list is exact and case-sensitive, each entry as it is written. To begin with an entry is a plain prefix: no word end is needed after it. What a round bracket holds, the container, and the text before and after a mark are the template's c.group, c.container, c.before and c.after.
definitions.first_match: For each mark the shapes are tried in the order they stand in this file, and the first whose test holds names the occurrence; so each test speaks only of occurrences that no shape above it, for the same mark, has taken.
definitions.pieces: The pieces of a text: cut the whole text at every comma and every semicolon that stands at the top level (the round bracket is the only bracket kind this dictionary uses, so a mark is at the top level when the opening round brackets before it are not more than the closing ones before it; every text that reaches a test on pieces balances, because an unbalanced text is taken first), and trim each part. A part left empty is an empty piece. The first piece is the part before the first such mark; the later pieces are the rest. The core of a piece is the piece with any run of the characters period, exclamation mark and question mark at its end removed, then trimmed. The first letter character of a piece is its first character that is neither the left single quotation mark (U+2018) nor an opening round bracket; a piece begins with an uppercase (or lowercase) letter when that character is one.
definitions.note_text: A text holds a pointer or note sign when it holds the three characters cmp. (c, m, p, period) anywhere, or the two characters &c anywhere, or has a piece whose trimmed text is exactly v. (the letter v and a period).
definitions.joining_text: A text has a joining piece when a later piece's first run of letters (the maximal run of letters at the start of the piece, empty if it does not begin with a letter) is an entry of joining_words.
definitions.leaning_text: A text has a leaning piece when some piece's core is an entry of leaning_pieces, or begins with an entry of leaning_pieces that is exactly 60 characters long (the long pieces are cut to their first 60 characters, so that no entry quotes more than 60 characters of the source).
definitions.term_piece: A piece is a term when its core holds no whitespace and is not empty, the piece itself is not an entry of grammar_labels, and one of these holds: its first letter character is an uppercase letter; or its core holds a letter that is none of A to Z, a to z, æ, œ, Æ and Œ, or holds the right single quotation mark (U+2019) or the left single quotation mark (U+2018); or its core is an entry of plain_terms.
definitions.name_text: A text has a name before its description when some piece is a term and the piece directly after it (the next piece, which exists) begins with a lowercase letter.
definitions.name_phrase_text: A text has a name phrase before its description when some piece's core holds two or more words (runs of non-whitespace characters) and the last of them has an uppercase letter as its first letter character, and the piece directly after it (which exists) has as its first run of letters a, an or the.
definitions.use_note_text: A text holds a note on use when some piece's first run of letters is use, one or more whitespace characters stand directly after that run, and the run of letters that begins directly after them is of (use of the root, use of the verb, use of the stem).
definitions.capitalised_text: A text is capitalised when every piece that is not empty begins with an uppercase letter.
definitions.wording_text: A text is a list of wordings when every piece that is not empty has as its first character a letter, the left single quotation mark (U+2018) or an opening round bracket.
definitions.label_after: A mark stands before a trailing grammar label when the text after the mark, trimmed, is an entry of grammar_labels.

homonyms.entry_identity: the pointed headword in the row's headwords field, outside the route text
homonyms.reason: The route text carries no entry number and no sense number, but the row carries a headwords field with the source's pointed headword: 112,003 of 115,918 rows (axis: rows) under 25,140 keys (axis: keys), and 3,614 keys carry more than one distinct pointed headword (the example key אדר carries 5), so the headword tells those entries apart; two entries the source points alike it does not. The source's own file gives every entry an id (rid) and numbers homonymous headwords with a superscript figure (the dump writes them as א ², א ³), which the overlay dropped together with the sense number. keys_with_more_than_one_route_text counts senses and homonyms together.

branches.question: This dictionary gives each sense its own row, and inside a row it parts groups of wordings with a semicolon, like: lofty; ruler, lord; proud, haughty. Each group is a shade of the one sense. Does the semicolon divide, so that each group prints as a pill of its own? (The commas inside a group are the next question, B02.)

options.means: Each semicolon between two groups of wordings divides: every group prints as its own pill, and the commas inside a group follow B02. A semicolon that ends a row, opens it, stands before a grammar label, or stands in a row with a note sign, a joining piece or a note on use (use of the verb) is not in this question and stays as written.
The row prints whole, as written, semicolons and all.

branches.question: Inside a row this dictionary parts the wordings of one sense with commas, like: to cut off, surround, isolate. Two spellings of a name stand the same way (Arbel, Arbela), and under one key each a colon and a full stop stand where such a comma would (to run: to pursue). Does each such comma divide, so that every wording prints as a pill of its own? If B01 keeps the semicolons whole, a semicolon stays inside its piece. The cost of divides: of 40 marks drawn uniformly from B02's 66,258 in v153 (seed 20261108), 2 were cut wrongly, 5 in 100 (95% range 1.4 to 16.5): a note on use (rejoicing, use of the root), now held whole, and a wording whose start the overlay's cut dropped (key אחז).

options.means: Each comma between two wordings of one sense divides, and so do the one colon and the one full stop that stand where such a comma would: every wording prints as its own pill, a final stop or cry sign staying with its wording. When B01 keeps the semicolons whole, a semicolon stays inside the piece it is written in, so that piece prints with the semicolon as written. A comma that ends a row, opens it, follows a leading grammar label, or stands in a row with a note sign, a joining piece, a hand-listed leaning piece, a note on use (use of the root) or a name or name phrase beside its description is not in this question and stays as written.
The row prints whole, as written, commas and all.

branches.question: A few rows carry a grammar label at one end of the wordings: a verb stem before them (Hif., to cause to pass; to remove) or a form note after them, behind a dash, a semicolon or a full stop (wild fig.—Pl.). The label is no reading. Should the page print the wordings without the label?

options.means: The row prints as written, label and all.

The page prints only the wordings: what stands after the comma of a leading label, or before the dash, semicolon or full stop that leads to a trailing label; a stop or colon that the wording itself ends in stays as written, and any division that B01 or B02 rules applies inside what is printed.

not_done_here: This ledger leaves to the overlay's own cut the edges of its rows. builder/store-questions.jsonl lists 737 texts (2,840 rows) whose edge the cut left wrong: a hanging comma, semicolon, hyphen, dash or colon at the end, a mark at the opening, a stranded initial or abbreviation (R. D., the Great S.), a pointer whose target was cut away (to moisten, v.), a stray closing bracket, a wording whose start the cut dropped (named by reading), or a grammar label and nothing else (Part. pass, Hif.;). In 685 of those texts (2,268 rows) the row's wording stands: only the mark at its end or opening, or the pointer, belongs to the cut, and that is the store's question; the other 52 hold no run of two or more letters but labels and abbreviations. The marks inside a listed row have their shapes like any other row's (266 listed texts carry a mark of B02 and 28 a mark of B01), so a branch answered divides cuts them too. Nothing is struck; a pointer at the end of a text stays in the last piece; and the hand list leaning_pieces names the pieces the builder read as leaning, so a piece may be moved later.
